title: Magnetic fields
examples: How do I draw the lines around a magnet?
What are the poles of a magnet?
Does the Earth have a magnetic field?

explain.say: Today we are learning about magnetic fields around magnets.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a bar magnet. Look at the north pole, the south pole and the field lines. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Magnetic field lines show the invisible force around a magnet.
The lines always go from a north pole to a south pole.
A magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole.
The Earth acts like a giant magnet with its own field.
Everyday life uses this field when we use a compass.

faq.q: Do the field lines cross each other anywhere?
faq.a: No, magnetic field lines never cross each other. If they crossed, it would mean the magnetic force was pulling in two different directions at the same point.
asks: Is it possible for lines to intersect?

faq.q: Is the Earth's magnetic field the same as a regular magnet?
faq.a: It is similar, but the Earth's field is huge and surrounds the whole planet. It helps protect us from space radiation.

faq.q: Do I need to draw arrows on the field lines?
faq.a: Yes, it is best to draw arrows on the field lines. The arrows show the direction of the force, from North to South.
asks: Which way do the lines go?

faq.q: Does a magnet have a North pole and a South pole?
faq.a: Yes, every magnet has two poles. These are the points where the magnetic field seems strongest.
asks: What are the ends of a magnet?
How many poles does a magnet have?

faq.a: Compasses work because the Earth's magnetic field lines pass through them. The needle lines up with the Earth's field.
asks: How does a compass find north?
What causes the needle to point north?

facts: Magnetic field lines are imaginary lines used to show the direction of a magnetic force.
Field lines always travel from the North pole to the South pole outside the magnet.
The Earth generates a magnetic field that surrounds our planet.
A compass needle points towards the Earth's magnetic North Pole.

quiz.say: If you draw field lines, where must they start?
quiz.why: The rule states that lines leave the North pole and enter the South pole.

wrong.0: The direction is always consistent, following the N to S path.
wrong.2: This is wrong because lines enter the South pole, they do not start there.
wrong.3: The field lines must start at one of the poles, not in the middle.

quiz.say: What does the Earth's magnetic field do for us?
quiz.why: The Earth's magnetic field acts like a shield against harmful space energy.

wrong.0: The field surrounds the entire planet, not just the poles.
wrong.1: It affects all magnetic materials, not just metal.
wrong.3: The field lines guide the compass to point generally north.

quiz.say: If you put two North poles near each other, what happens?
quiz.why: Like poles, such as North and North, always push each other away.

wrong.0: Repulsion is the force when the poles are the same.
wrong.2: Opposite poles attract, but like poles always repel.
wrong.3: There is a strong magnetic force acting between them.
